title: Tag every issue-body dependency entry as prereq, merged, sibling, or parallel

facts.note: Issue bodies are tracker content, not repository files. An observer must expose the issue body being authored, edited, reviewed, or validated.
The rule is an invariant on issue-body content. It applies whenever an issue body with Dependencies #N entries is checked, including existing bodies that nobody is editing.
Task wording is only a hint that an issue body with dependencies is in scope. It does not prove that the artifact exists.
Validator finding for a #N entry in a Dependencies section whose tag is missing or is not one of prereq/merged/sibling/parallel.

fires: A new issue body has a Dependencies section that lists one or more #N references
A #N entry is added to, or changed in, the Dependencies section of an existing issue body
An existing issue body is reviewed or validated and its Dependencies section has #N entries, even when nobody edits it
A #N entry in a Dependencies section has no trailing tag
A #N entry in a Dependencies section has a trailing marker that is not exactly one of prereq, merged, sibling, or parallel
doesNotFire: #N references that appear outside the Dependencies section, e.g. in the narrative or graph-context sections
An issue body that has no Dependencies section or no #N entries in it
Code, tests, or docs that are not issue bodies

given: An issue body has a Dependencies section containing '#N' references (dependency entries), whether new or already present
when: That issue body is authored, edited, reviewed, or validated
then: Every #N dependency entry must carry a trailing classification tag that is exactly one of: prereq, merged, sibling, or parallel.
prefer: Put the classification as a trailing marker on each #N entry

Use prereq for work that must merge before this issue can proceed and merged for a prereq that has already landed. Use sibling or parallel for related work that runs alongside this issue and is not waited on. The source does not distinguish sibling from parallel, so either tag satisfies the rule for such work.
When an existing issue body has untagged or wrongly tagged entries, fix the tags on those entries
avoid: Leaving any #N entry untagged, or using a tag other than prereq/merged/sibling/parallel
Dropping or moving real dependencies out of the Dependencies section just to avoid having to classify them
why: Classifying each dependency prevents the session-template merge-wait loop from hanging on sibling or parallel work.
evidence: Validator test_issue_deps_have_classification_tags passes for the issue body
Each '#N' reference in the Dependencies section carries a trailing marker that is exactly one of prereq, merged, sibling, or parallel
verifier_detail: dependency_entry: a '#N' reference in the Dependencies section of an issue body
classification_tag: a trailing prereq/merged/sibling/parallel marker on the entry. The allowed set is closed: {prereq, merged, sibling, parallel}. Report both missing and invalid tags.
Disposition advisory, severity 2: findings are reported but are not blocking. Suppressions are allowed only until the suppression deadline of 2026-12-31.

additions.text: Tag guidance: prereq = must merge first; merged = a prereq that has already landed; sibling or parallel = related work that runs alongside and is not waited on. The source does not distinguish these two, so either is acceptable.
additions.justification: The source names the tags and says the merge-wait loop must not hang on sibling or parallel work, but it never defines them. The planner needs working meanings to choose a tag. The guidance adds no obligation and does not invent a sibling/parallel distinction that the source lacks.

additions.text: Fix the tags on untagged or wrongly tagged entries in existing issue bodies
additions.justification: This restates the invariant ('every entry') for bodies that already exist. It adds no new obligation.

additions.text: Dropping or moving real dependencies to avoid classifying them
additions.justification: The author instructions require guarding against gaming the validator. This adds no obligation beyond the statement.

additions.text: doesNotFire for #N references outside the Dependencies section; operations review/validate and invalid-tag situations
additions.justification: The scope follows from the dependency_entry term definition, which is limited to the Dependencies section. Review/validate and invalid tags follow from the statement being an invariant over every entry with a closed tag set.

trace.note: rationale kept verbatim in meaning; no stronger causal claim is made elsewhere
